name: Gemini Robotics 2
summary: Gemini Robotics 2 extends DeepMind's VLA line from tabletop bimanual manipulation to whole-body humanoid control, issuing coordinated commands for locomotion and manipulation from one model — walking to a table, picking up a watering can, stepping to a shelf and placing it, from a single natural-language instruction. It ships in three variants: the Gemini Robotics 2 VLA for control, Gemini Robotics ER 2 for embodied reasoning, task planning and multi-robot coordination, and Gemini Robotics On-Device 2 for local deployment. The release adds multi-finger dexterity, multi-robot collaboration, and adaptation to a new embodiment in a few hours. DeepMind reports 45.7-76.3% success on whole-body manipulation tasks, 74.2-89.6% on gripper dexterity and 32-92% on multi-finger tasks depending on complexity. The whole-body demonstrations run on Apptronik's Apollo 2.
innovation: Locomotion and manipulation emitted by one policy rather than a manipulation model riding on a separate walking controller.
The ER variant graduates from single-robot planning to coordinating several robots on one task.
matters: Removes the tabletop assumption that has bounded the VLA literature since RT-1, and does it on a commercial humanoid.
limits: Closed: early-access partners and private preview only, with no weights, code or independent reproduction.
Multi-finger success spans 32-92%, so the dexterity claim rests heavily on which task you look at.
lineage: Gemini Robotics 1.5's embodied reasoning plus action, extended to the whole body.
